AES_cbc_encrypt.notes: openHiTLS provides public CBC cipher APIs through CRYPT_EAL_Cipher*, but not OpenSSL's low-level AES_KEY-based CBC helper.  [DEPRECATED in OpenSSL 3.0+; migration required regardless of hitls availability] ⚠ return convention: openHiTLS int-returning functions use CRYPT_SUCCESS=0 for success (errnos nonzero); OpenSSL commonly uses 1=success / 0=failure. Check error-handling idioms when substituting.

HMAC.notes: One-shot HMAC is realizable through the public MAC pipeline, but openHiTLS has no single OpenSSL-shaped helper function. ⚠ return convention: openHiTLS int-returning functions use CRYPT_SUCCESS=0 for success (errnos nonzero); OpenSSL commonly uses 1=success / 0=failure. Check error-handling idioms when substituting.

HMAC_CTX_copy.notes: Public MAC context copy exists, but digest selection remains baked into the generic MAC ctx construction path.  [DEPRECATED in OpenSSL 3.0+; migration required regardless of hitls availability] ⚠ return convention: openHiTLS int-returning functions use CRYPT_SUCCESS=0 for success (errnos nonzero); OpenSSL commonly uses 1=success / 0=failure. Check error-handling idioms when substituting.

HMAC_CTX_free.notes: Direct, void-returning, null-safe MAC context free.  [DEPRECATED in OpenSSL 3.0+; migration required regardless of hitls availability]

HMAC_CTX_get_md.notes: No public MAC ctx API returns the configured digest algorithm as an EVP_MD-like object.

HMAC_CTX_new.notes: openHiTLS requires a concrete CRYPT_MAC_HMAC_* algorithm ID at ctx creation, while OpenSSL creates an untyped HMAC ctx and defers digest selection to HMAC_Init_ex.  [DEPRECATED in OpenSSL 3.0+; migration required regardless of hitls availability]

HMAC_CTX_reset.notes: Public deinit and reinit exist, but the reset contract stays on generic MAC ctx rather than HMAC_CTX.  [DEPRECATED in OpenSSL 3.0+; migration required regardless of hitls availability] ⚠ return convention: openHiTLS int-returning functions use CRYPT_SUCCESS=0 for success (errnos nonzero); OpenSSL commonly uses 1=success / 0=failure. Check error-handling idioms when substituting.

HMAC_CTX_set_flags.notes: No public HMAC flag-control surface exists; documented MacCtrl parameters cover GMAC-specific knobs only.

HMAC_Final.notes: Maps to MacFinal. Call flow: ctx->method.final dispatches to CRYPT_HMAC_Final.  [DEPRECATED in OpenSSL 3.0+; migration required regardless of hitls availability] ⚠ return convention: openHiTLS int-returning functions use CRYPT_SUCCESS=0 for success (errnos nonzero); OpenSSL commonly uses 1=success / 0=failure. HMAC_Init.notes: Key initialization exists, but the digest was already fixed when the HMAC MAC ctx was created. ⚠ return convention: openHiTLS int-returning functions use CRYPT_SUCCESS=0 for success (errnos nonzero); OpenSSL commonly uses 1=success / 0=failure. MD5_Final.notes: WARNING: NOT drop-in. openHiTLS has no split Init/Update/Final hash pipeline matching the OpenSSL legacy low-level API. SHA1_Final.notes: WARNING: NOT drop-in. openHiTLS has no split Init/Update/Final hash pipeline matching the OpenSSL legacy low-level API. The cited CRYPT_EAL_MdNewCtx + MdInit [+ MdUpdate [+ MdFinal]] chain is a full one-shot recipe; naive substitution for SHAx_Update will leak contexts, and SHAx_Init/Final alone will skip allocation/deallocation. Either refactor caller to one-shot CRYPT_EAL_Md or wrap with a custom facade that preserves the Init/Update/Final streaming contract.
